firms.email_text: Private Wealth Partners stood out for its depth of tenure and the genuine long-term orientation Bill brings to client relationships. Over 30 years building this firm and its predecessor, along with a career that spans institutional trading and portfolio management, reflects a practitioner-first culture that is increasingly rare. The firm's concentrated, relationship-driven approach to UHNW families and charitable organizations is exactly the kind of model we take seriously in our work.

Intellectus caught our attention for its intentional focus on entrepreneurs and innovators whose wealth is deeply tied to their business interests. The founders' backgrounds at Deutsche Bank and Lehman Brothers, combined with active involvement in Silicon Valley venture-stage companies, reflect a platform built to engage clients at every stage of wealth creation, not just after liquidity. The multi-family office model supported by Dynasty is a thoughtful infrastructure choice.

Mission Creek stood out for its specialized focus on concentrated equity positions and post-venture transition planning. Helping clients navigate complex balance sheet decisions, including private equity distributions and single-stock strategies, requires both technical depth and client trust. The firm's sub-advisory work for other advisors and family offices further signals a quality of work that earns respect from peers in the industry.

Blume Capital's longevity and research-driven investment philosophy caught our attention immediately. Three decades managing portfolios for individuals, families, and foundations with a value-oriented, non-institutional approach reflects a culture of genuine conviction. The firm's depth of relationship with clients seeking personalized counsel, rather than off-the-shelf solutions, is something we consistently see in durable advisory businesses.

Stewart Wealth Management stood out for the straightforward, client-first culture Ben has built since founding the firm in 2007. A fee-only, planning-led model for Marin and Bay Area families, with a real emphasis on long-term partnership rather than product, reflects a strong point of view on what independent advisory should look like. Firms built around one clear vision and sustained over time are the ones we find most interesting.

Ohana stood out for its referral-only model and its 25-year track record serving ultra-high-net-worth families with genuine multi-family-office depth. The combination of institutional-quality manager selection, direct investments, estate planning, family office administration, and philanthropic advisory in a boutique setting is uncommon. Firms that grow entirely through relationship trust rather than marketing often have the strongest client alignment.

REMP stood out for its multi-decade continuity and its life planning orientation. Four partners, each with 25 or more years with the firm, representing a level of institutional consistency that clients can rely on across generations. The referral-only model and the deliberate balance of investment management with comprehensive personal planning reflects a culture built around service quality, not growth for its own sake.

Lyell stood out immediately. The founding story, four partners leaving Atherton Lane together to build something on their own terms, reflects strong alignment and a shared point of view on how wealth management should be practiced. The depth of planning around executive compensation, RSUs, and liquidity events, paired with a boutique investment approach, positions the firm well for the clients it serves across the Peninsula.

DiversiFi caught our attention for its focused specialization in equity compensation planning for Bay Area tech professionals. RSUs, stock options, AMT planning, and concentrated position management require real expertise, and the virtual advisory model allows the firm to serve clients wherever their careers take them. Firms with clear positioning in a well-defined client segment tend to earn deep loyalty and strong referral pipelines.

Elevation Wealth Partners stood out for its genuine integration of investment management with in-house tax preparation and accounting. Offering CPA services alongside portfolio management, rather than simply referring clients elsewhere, reflects a commitment to coordinated advice that clients in the Bay Area genuinely benefit from. Barry's 30-plus years in financial services and his community involvement, including founding the Cancer Support Community's endowment fund, signal a leader who thinks long-term.

Silicon Valley Capital Partners stood out for its proprietary, research-driven investment process. The combination of a top-down macroeconomic framework with bottom-up valuation and momentum modeling, documented in a published research report, reflects intellectual rigor that goes well beyond typical RIA portfolio construction. Serving affluent Silicon Valley clients across investment management, insurance, and charitable giving for over two decades signals real staying power.

Karen's background caught our attention immediately. A CPA with an MBA, CFP, and PFS, combined with 20-plus years advising Silicon Valley executives through IPOs, acquisitions, and complex compensation packages, is a rare combination. The firm's reputation as a thought leader on stock option planning, reflected in national publications and her service on AICPA's Personal Financial Planning Executive Committee, speaks to both technical depth and professional standing.

Frank, Rimerman Advisors stands apart from most RIAs we encounter in our work. The affiliation with Silicon Valley's largest independent CPA firm creates a genuinely integrated platform for UHNW entrepreneurs and executives who need investment management and tax advisory working in concert, not in parallel. The concentration of client relationships at very high average size reflects a selectivity that earns trust.

Neumann Capital stood out for its collaborative team culture and the CFA-led investment discipline at its core. Founded in 1992 and built around long-standing client relationships, the firm represents a fee-only model that has earned loyalty over more than three decades. Firms of this tenure with a consistent philosophy and a multi-advisor team often have the most thoughtful views on continuity and long-term stewardship.

Wealth Architects stood out for its purpose-driven approach and the breadth of the multi-shareholder team Mark built since founding in 2008. Integrating financial planning with insurance, tax, estate, real estate, and philanthropic giving, all explicitly values-aligned, reflects a vision of comprehensive advisory that goes well beyond investment management. The firm's YMCA and community board involvement reinforces a culture of long-term thinking beyond just portfolio returns.

Spiegelman Wealth caught our attention for its generational story and the deliberate independence Adam chose in launching his own RIA in 2025. Taking over a family practice after years of relationship-building, then choosing to build something under your own terms rather than joining a larger platform, reflects a strong point of view on client service. The firm's specialization in clients within five years of retirement, focusing on the how and when rather than just the how much, is a meaningful distinction.

FFG stood out for the strength of its multi-credential team and its integration of CPA services with investment advisory. A CFP and CPA-led firm offering in-house tax reporting and planning alongside evidence-based portfolio management reflects exactly the kind of coordinated advisory model that Bay Area executives and tech professionals find valuable. The firm's growth since 2016 across multiple offices signals real momentum.

Traveka caught our attention for its clarity and focus. Launching an independent RIA after years at Goldman Sachs Personal Financial Management and United Capital, and building it around a defined niche in Silicon Valley tech professionals with complex equity compensation, reflects a very intentional vision. Tony's CFA and CFP credentials, combined with Dynasty's infrastructure, position the firm well for disciplined, long-term growth.

Elmwood stood out for the partnership Bob and Shannon built after leaving institutional asset management to serve Bay Area technology professionals on their own terms. The all-inclusive service model, where every client gets the full team, reflects a culture that prioritizes depth over scale. The specialization in equity compensation, RSUs, tender offers, and QSBS alongside comprehensive financial planning positions the firm well for the client base it serves.

Blueprint stood out for its deliberate concentration and the caliber of experience Bob brings to the practice. A Harvard MBA, early career spanning Morgan Stanley, Boston Consulting Group, and private equity, followed by building a boutique RIA focused on a small number of high-quality client relationships, reflects a very intentional philosophy. Founders who prioritize depth over headcount often have the clearest sense of what they are building and why.

What drew us to Clarity Wealth Advisors was its depth of experience and genuine client-first philosophy. Building an independent, fee-only practice and sustaining it for over a decade reflects the kind of intentional culture we take seriously. Deep advisory experience, fee-only independence, and real roots in the local community all point to a practice built around long-term relationships rather than transactional growth.

Capital Trust impressed us with the depth and tenure of its team. A disciplined investment process spanning commercial lending, fixed income, and portfolio management brings an institutional rigor you rarely see in a boutique setting. The team's emphasis on multi-generational planning, privacy, and high-touch responsiveness for affluent families reflects a culture built on earned trust rather than scale.

Two things stand out about Avalon: its intellectual rigor and the longevity of its founding partnership. Deep roots in quantitative research — including the firm's proprietary “Ada” dynamic allocation model and an advisory relationship with Ned Davis Research — reflect a systematic discipline uncommon in boutique wealth management. A firm co-founded in 1992 that has kept evolving its process while maintaining a curated client base is worth a serious conversation.

Everest's founding story is what stayed with us — a firm built specifically to close the gaps in financial services that Silicon Valley professionals so often run into. That kind of origin is something clients can feel. The focus on first-generation high earners navigating complex, multi-account wealth — RSUs, 401(k)s, brokerage accounts, real estate — is a well-defined niche, and the kind of focus that earns real loyalty.

Three Bridge is on our radar for its serious positioning at the top of the Silicon Valley market. Deep expertise in alternative investments and national media visibility reflect the credibility it has earned among entrepreneurs, venture capitalists, and executives with average client assets near $23M. A personal-CFO service model and a white-glove approach to client experience add up to exactly the kind of comprehensive platform that resonates with clients at that level.

Opes interested us for the way it integrates real estate advisory into the wealth management relationship. Roots in West Coast real estate development paired with deep investment-management experience give the firm a genuine edge with Apple and Silicon Valley executives weighing equity compensation alongside real property decisions. A culture that promotes from within — turning clients into partners — signals a firm that earns deep trust, inside and out.

Rosenblum Silverman Sutton has a remarkable institutional history, and that's what first caught our attention. Founded in 1984 around independently developed investment disciplines, the firm carries a legacy of conviction and independence that's genuinely rare. More than 40 years of continuity serving HNW families, trusts, and foundations is a testament to a culture built on trust and results.

Chequers came up in our research for its clear positioning at the intersection of law, tax, and wealth management. Deep professional roots across law, tax, and institutional wealth management — paired with a recognized voice on tax and wealth — earn it credibility with entrepreneurs and executives navigating genuinely complex tax, liquidity, and estate decisions. The firm's rapid growth and recognition as one of the fastest-growing RIAs in the country signals strong client resonance.

We were struck by the institutional pedigree of the Atlas investment team and the seriousness of its process. Deep institutional investment experience — including large-scale corporate treasury and CIO-level portfolio management — brings a level of rigor rarely found in independent advisory. A systematic, multi-factor equity strategy, with all four principals holding the CFA designation, reflects a firm built around conviction in process over personality.

What makes Flywheel interesting to us is the deliberateness of its founding. Launching a fee-only, fiduciary RIA in 2023 — built on years of client-relationship experience at major institutions, and designed as a boutique rather than a scale play — reflects a strong point of view on what wealth management should look like. Firms founded with a clear vision of client experience, rather than a headcount target, are the ones we find most interesting.

McCarthy Asset Management earned a spot on our list for its tightly integrated CPA and advisory model. Launching an investment management practice in 1999, in direct response to what clients were asking for, points to a firm shaped around real needs rather than a market opportunity. Deep technical grounding across tax, accounting, and financial planning adds up to the kind of planning integration that clients managing retirement transitions genuinely benefit from.

Brickley caught our eye for the integration of its CPA and investment advisory roots and the multi-generational depth it has built with professional families. Beginning as a tax practice in 1985 and expanding into investment advisory in 1999, the firm has earned trust through technical credibility rather than marketing. The client base — CPA and law-firm partners, biotech and software executives, trust and estate beneficiaries — signals a firm that handles genuinely complex planning relationships over long time horizons.

Jackson Square is high on our list for its positioning at the ultra-high-net-worth end of the market. Deep institutional portfolio-management experience, applied to a highly selective client base, gives the firm a foundation you don't often see at boutique scale. Launching an independent firm in 2019 to serve that segment on its own terms — rather than inside a bank platform — says a lot about how personalized service at that level ought to work.

Gordian stands out to us for a distinctive combination of institutional markets experience and independent advisory practice. A foundation in institutional markets and analytical consulting brings a rigorous, research-driven approach to client wealth management. Building an independent RIA in the Marin corridor with a focus on HNW professionals and pre-retirees speaks to a deliberate choice to build something client-centered and durable.

Asset Dedication stood out for the intellectual originality of its founding. Built on an academic, decision-sciences foundation — and an investment platform centered on bond laddering and dedicated portfolios for retirement income — the firm reflects a rare convergence of academic rigor and practical application. A firm managing nearly $3B built on proprietary methodology rather than off-the-shelf allocation models is worth a conversation.

Destination stood out for its longevity and national profile. Founded in 1986 — one of the oldest independent RIAs in the Bay Area — and sustained for nearly 40 years with consistent recognition from Barron's as a top independent advisor, it's a firm with genuine staying power. A strong academic orientation signals a firm that takes the intellectual side of wealth management seriously.

Sivia caught our attention for an unconventional founding path and its positioning at the top of the UHNW market. An entrepreneurial, operator's background — spanning building and exiting companies before launching a multi-family office with a $10M minimum — maps directly onto the startup-to-exit client cycle Sivia serves. Firms built by people who have lived the wealth-creation journey tend to earn a different kind of client trust.

Creekside caught our attention for its distinctive community orientation and the deliberate regional focus it has maintained since founding in 2008. A firm that integrates educational seminars and workshops into its practice alongside financial planning and portfolio management reflects a culture of genuine outreach, not just client service. Independent advisory businesses with strong community roots in specific geographies tend to build the kind of client loyalty that sustains them across generations.

Ridgecrest caught our attention for the scale the firm has built since founding in 2021. Over $700M in AUM and 744 accounts from a three-person team in just a few years points to real operational discipline and a clear client value proposition. Early-stage firms that hit that kind of traction usually have a strong prior client base behind them and a very clear sense of what they're building.

Fairview stood out for its multi-generational continuity and the depth it has built over nearly 30 years of independent practice. Decades of seasoned investment experience — now carried day-to-day by the next generation of the family — add up to a genuine succession story and a firm built for the long term. Employee-owned advisory businesses with family continuity and a $2M minimum often have the most durable client relationships in the industry.

Financial Avengers caught our attention for the focused practice it has built in the East Bay. A lean operation serving individuals and small businesses across more than 200 accounts reflects a strong client-service ethos without the overhead of a large platform. Independent practices grown on their own terms, without institutional backing, often have the clearest sense of what clients need — and what a partnership should look like.

Capital Advantage stood out for its longevity and the scale it has built independently in the East Bay. Founded in 1998 and sustained through multiple market cycles, a practice managing over $1.25B reflects real client loyalty and consistent delivery across more than 25 years. Independent firms with that kind of track record in the Walnut Creek corridor are exactly what we look at seriously as Sequoia considers Bay Area expansion.

Westend caught our attention for its growth trajectory and the concentrated client base it has built in Marin since founding in 2002. A 150% net-new-assets growth rate and 63% revenue growth signal a practice with real momentum, not just steady-state maintenance. Firms growing organically at that pace usually have a compelling client value proposition and a clear sense of what they're building toward.

Occidental stood out for its genuinely differentiated positioning around behavioral finance. A foundation in deep-value investing and applied behavioral economics — combined with nationally recognized expertise in financial therapy — reflects a firm that has built real intellectual infrastructure around client decision-making, not just portfolio construction. The “Your Mental Wealth Advisors” brand points to a conviction that's uncommon and increasingly relevant.

Bell Investment Advisors caught our attention for the depth of practice it has built in the East Bay over more than 25 years. A firm managing nearly $800M across 443 accounts, with a broad service menu spanning individuals, institutions, and pension consulting, reflects a generalist practice built on consistent client relationships. Independent advisory businesses with that kind of tenure and scale in the Orinda corridor are exactly what we look at as Sequoia evaluates Bay Area expansion.

Sentry stood out for the remarkable concentration and scale of its client relationships. A four-person firm managing over $2.4B, with average client assets near $13M, reflects a highly selective practice built around institutional-quality clients rather than volume. That kind of per-client density — uncommon at any firm size — typically reflects both deep trust and a very deliberate approach to who the firm chooses to serve.

Greykasell caught our attention for the scale it brought in at launch. Registering in 2024 with over $443M in AUM from the outset points to an experienced team that built a substantial client following before making the move to independence. Breakaway practices with that kind of initial traction reflect strong client loyalty and a clear vision for what an independent practice should look like — and we'd welcome a conversation about where the firm goes from here.

One Wealth stood out for a distinctive founding philosophy and the breadth of what's been built since the team left J.P. Morgan together in 2014. A “Financial Life Planning” model that treats financial and personal wellbeing as genuinely inseparable — supported by Dynasty's infrastructure and grown to over $1.25B — reflects a vision that goes well beyond investment management. An entrepreneurial spirit runs through how the firm approaches client relationships, too.

Sage Rhino caught our attention for the range of investment experience behind its client portfolios. Deep alternative and institutional investment experience — across traditional portfolio management and market-neutral strategies — is rarely found in an independent RIA. A firm managing nearly $900M across equities, fixed income, private funds, real estate, and digital assets has genuinely broad investment capability.

Navigation Group caught our attention for the growth it has achieved on the Peninsula since founding in 2017. Over $1B in AUM and 342 clients across a six-advisor team reflects a practice that has built real scale while staying client-centric. Independent advisory firms on that kind of growth trajectory often have a compelling client proposition and a clear sense of where the practice is going.

Sand Hill stood out for its institutional investment infrastructure and deep roots in the Silicon Valley ecosystem. Deep institutional portfolio-management experience — combined with an employee-owned structure and an ESG-integrated, open-architecture investment approach — reflects a firm that has built real credibility serving entrepreneurs, executives, and foundations in the Valley for decades.

TTP caught our attention for the focused practice it has built in the South Bay since founding in 2016. Managing over $570M across 382 client relationships reflects a practice that has earned steady trust in the San Jose market. Independent firms that build a solid, growing book in a specific geography over nearly a decade typically have strong client relationships and a clear sense of what they're building toward.

RPG caught our attention for the operational scale the team has achieved in the Tri-Valley market. Nearly $1.05B in AUM across 953 client relationships reflects both efficiency and breadth — a model that serves a wide range of individuals and small businesses with consistent delivery. Independent firms with that kind of account depth and a nine-person team in the East Bay have typically built strong community roots and real referral infrastructure.

Verita stood out immediately for its positioning at the very top of the UHNW market. Senior leadership pedigree from the upper tiers of banking and investment management — now channeled into an independent practice with an average client relationship exceeding $59M — reflects a clear conviction about what ultra-high-net-worth clients deserve and a platform designed to deliver it. The 2025 launch signals something intentional, built from a position of strength.

Van Strum & Towne stood out for something simple and increasingly rare: longevity. A firm founded in 1976 — now approaching 50 years — managing nearly $500M for a select group of HNW individuals and families in San Francisco reflects decades of consistent client trust. Practices that have survived and served clients across that many market cycles have built something that cannot be replicated. We’d welcome a conversation about the firm’s future and whether Sequoia’s platform might be worth exploring.

firms.firm_name: The Pacific Center For Financial Services
firms.email_text: The Pacific Center caught our attention for the depth of practice it has built in the Tri-Valley since founding in 1997. Nearly three decades of independent advisory work managing close to $1B for individuals and small businesses in the San Ramon corridor reflects consistent delivery and a genuine client following. Independent practices with that kind of tenure in the East Bay have typically built the embedded relationships and referral networks that create real long-term value.

Vantage stood out for its equal five-way partnership structure and the scale the team has built together on the Peninsula. Managing over $1.1B with 639 accounts and nine staff reflects a collaborative model that has delivered consistent growth. Five-partner advisory firms with that kind of shared ownership and geographic focus often have the most thoughtful conversations about continuity and long-term stewardship — and those are exactly the conversations Sequoia is built for.

North Berkeley caught our attention for the culture it has built and its clear sense of place in the East Bay. Managing over $830M with a 16-person team, grounded in the Berkeley community, reflects a practice that has grown by earning deep trust with clients who share a values-aligned approach to wealth. Independent advisory firms with strong community identity and a multi-person team tend to have the most durable client relationships — and the most interesting conversations about what comes next.

Vernal Point stood out for the rarity of its positioning and the depth of expertise behind it. A firm purpose-built around single-family-office design and management for UHNW global families — with a $250,000 annual minimum and 20 client relationships averaging nearly $200M each — reflects a genuinely specialized practice. Multiple advanced credentials and repeated industry recognition reflect an investment in professional excellence that clients at that level demand.

Westhill caught our attention for its 35-year track record and the thoughtful succession it has put in place. Co-founded in 1989, rebranded as Westhill in 2021, and now elevating a new President in 2026 after nearly a decade of internal development, it's a firm that has clearly thought about what comes next. Advisory practices with that kind of tenure in Marin, combined with deliberate next-generation leadership, are exactly the conversations Sequoia is designed to support.

firms.firm_name: Werba Rubin Papier Wealth Management, LLC
firms.email_text: Werba Rubin Papier stood out for the strength of its three-partner founding model and the scale the team has built in the South Bay. Equal-thirds ownership among three co-founders managing over $1.4B with 677 client relationships reflects a deep alignment of interests and a practice built on genuine partnership. The Buckingham Strategic Partners affiliation signals an evidence-based investment philosophy that clients increasingly value. One of the leading independent RIAs in the South Bay by any measure, and a firm we wanted to make sure was part of our outreach.
